name: Schloss Lengberg
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Lengberg in Nikolsdorf (Osttirol): monumental 12th-century Renaissance fortress on a dolomite rock, renowned for late medieval bra discoveries.
beschreibung:
Overview

The formidable Schloss Lengberg perches proudly atop a striking, wooded hill overlooking the Drau valley in the municipality of Nikolsdorf in the Osttirol district of Lienz, at an altitude of approximately 715 metres. Situated just twelve kilometres east of the Dolomite town of Lienz near the border with Carinthia, this expansive complex forms one of the most historically significant fortified castles in the entire southern Tyrolean Alpine region. With its massive defensive curtain walls, Romanesque keep, and picturesque Renaissance courtyard, the castle unites more than 800 years of architectural and feudal history with groundbreaking scientific discoveries of international significance.

History & Archaeological Sensation

The origins of the stronghold date back to the late 12th century: around the year 1190, the Counts of Lechsgemünde had the defensive fortress constructed to guard the ancient trade route passing through the Drau valley. In the 15th century, Lengberg passed to the powerful Counts of Görz; the regional sovereign Virgil von Graben expanded the fortress from 1485 onwards in late Gothic style into a prestigious residence, commissioning the splendid castle chapel dedicated to Saints Sebastian and Nicholas. In the 16th century, the palas was enhanced with elegant Renaissance arcade galleries. In 2008, archaeologists from the Universität Innsbruck made a world-historic discovery during extensive restoration works: in a sealed 15th-century vault, over 2,700 textile fragments were unearthed – including the world's oldest surviving late medieval brassieres (dated to roughly 1440–1480). This discovery revolutionized European fashion history, as bras had previously been widely believed to have been invented only in the late 19th century. Since 1956, the castle has been owned by the State of Tyrol and is operated by the Aufbauwerk der Jugend as an exemplary educational and vocational training centre for young people.

Visit & Getting There

The exterior grounds of Schloss Lengberg, the grand approach avenue, and the picturesque castle courtyard are open year-round with free admission. The late Gothic castle chapel, featuring valuable winged altarpieces and historic murals, is open to visitors during the day. The historical interior state rooms are accessible during regular guided tours, special exhibitions, and musical concerts. Arrival by car: Via the Drautalstraße B100 from Lienz towards Spittal an der Drau to Nikolsdorf/Lengberg, taking the signposted turnoff up to the castle car park (free). By public transport: ÖBB trains (Drautalbahn) to Nikolsdorf station, from where a scenic footpath leads uphill to the castle gate in about 15 minutes.

Tips

From the castle courtyard and the south terrace, visitors are treated to a magnificent panoramic vista across the wide Drau valley basin and the jagged limestone crags of the Lienzer Dolomiten. Combine your visit with a stop at the nearby Lienz-Nikolsdorf airfield or take a stroll along the historic Roman trail down in the valley. During summer, the atmospheric castle courtyard serves as a stunning open-air venue for classical concerts and theatrical performances.
